description: The actual subject of docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md. Closed enums (NeutronicsFidelity, ThermalHydraulicFidelity) so adding a band is a compile error at every consumer; Arc<T> for heavyweight read-only pieces so size_of stays small (workspace Rust design rules: no dyn, no Box, no lifetimes). HANDOFF RULES: down-switch integrates conserved quantities over constituent fine cells (volume-weighted, NEVER arithmetic-mean); up-switch distributes the coarse total then RELAXES toward the fine profile over a few steps; total mass and energy before/after must agree to solver tolerance AS A TEST, not a comment; never switch inside a corrector loop. Precedents already working in-tree: PipeBackend (crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:25) and the HeaterType 8-vs-15-node runtime mesh switch (ciet_opcua/state.rs:68). Reuse the tested mesh_to_mesh.rs, rbf_mapping.rs and interpolate_table.rs from genfoam, which nothing in the digital-twin path currently calls.
title: engine: FidelityLevel enum with conservation-asserted state handoff

description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, second comment: 'Kovan should have a bibliography window which manages bib files like jabref. However, there should be more than jabref'). Depends on op-63u0 (project-folder design) and op-b1y5 (kovan.toml, which this window cross-references).

SCOPE: a GUI window/tab that opens and manages the project folder's single named .bib file -- list/search/edit entries, JabRef-like -- but grounded in the kovan.toml index rather than being a bare .bib editor: an entry in this window should be able to jump to its PDF (op-95x6's reader), its markdown sections (op-9c2e.13), and its digitised CSVs, via kovan.toml's pointers. That cross-referencing is the 'more than JabRef' the maintainer asked for -- a plain .bib table view alone does not satisfy this bead.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PARTIALLY implemented, deliberately scoped down -- see the module doc in crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/bibliography.rs for the full reasoning. The bead's core ask is a JabRef-like list/search/EDIT surface over .bib entries. This workspace has no BibTeX PARSER (only a renderer, kovan_literature::bibtex::to_bibtex, KovanDocument -> BibTeX one-way) -- flagged as op-vi1n when op-b1y5 hit the same gap. Without a parser there is no way to read an existing .bib file's entries into anything a GUI could list/search/edit, so that half of this bead is genuinely blocked on op-vi1n, not implemented here.

What IS implemented -- the 'more than JabRef' cross-referencing half, which needed no bib parsing (kovan.toml's own document list is enough): a new Bibliography tab (top bar) listing a project's documents (id + which of the 5 standard sections each has), a text filter, and per-row 'Open PDF' / 'Edit Markdown' buttons that jump to the PDF Reader / Markdown Editor tabs pre-loaded with that document (MarkdownEditorState::open_document, new). No .bib entry fields (title/authors/year) are shown or editable anywhere in this panel -- says so explicitly in its own module doc so a future reader doesn't mistake the cross-reference list for the bib editor the bead actually asked for.

Leaving this bead OPEN (not closed) since the core ask is not done -- re-open fully once op-vi1n lands a BibTeX parser. Verified: cargo check clean both targets, cargo test --release -p kovan clean (172+15+17+7 passing), cargo doc clean.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Update: op-vi1n (the missing BibTeX parser this bead's "manage .bib entries like JabRef" half was blocked on) is now done -- `kovan_literature::parse_bib_entries` exists and is already wired into `project.rs`'s cite-key join. The cross-referencing half of this bead (jump from a bib row to its PDF/markdown) is already implemented per the prior session's work. The remaining scope -- an actual in-GUI .bib entry editor (add/edit/delete entries, write back to the .bib file) -- is now technically unblocked but not implemented in this pass; it's a genuinely separate, sizeable GUI feature and wasn't part of the current explicit ask. Leaving this bead's status as-is (In Progress) rather than closing it, since that half is still open.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Both halves now complete via op-xj8t (the .bib entry editor, just closed). Closing this bead too.

title: kovan-gui: bibliography management window (JabRef-like, project-folder-aware)

description:
Two smaller sharp edges found 2026-08-11 in the full range-literal audit of region_fwd_eqn_single_phase done for op-cv1c. Neither is the op-cv1c defect and neither was changed by its fix (behaviour-only scope), but both are real.

1. p = 0 Pa is ACCEPTED, not rejected. The Region-2 arm's disjuncts use (0.0..=p_sat_reg4_pascal) and (0.0..=p_boundary_23_pascal) and (0.0..=100e6) — all START-INCLUSIVE at zero. IF97 is defined for p > 0 (the ideal-gas part of the Region-2 Gibbs function contains ln(pi), which diverges at p = 0), so a p = 0 call returns a non-finite value rather than panicking or erroring. The bounds-checked facade interfaces::checked already rejects p <= 0, so this only bites callers of the raw functions.
   Suggested fix: exclusive lower edges in the Region-2 arms, so p = 0 hits the router panic like any other out-of-envelope input. Behaviour change, needs its own test.

2. Doc/code contradiction on the B23 line. The doc comment on p_boundary_2_3 (region_3_.../aux_eqn_boundary_region_2_and_region_3.rs:4) says 'note that points ON this line belong to region 2'. But the router's Region-3 arm is (p_boundary_23_pascal..=100e6), start-INCLUSIVE, and it is matched BEFORE the Region-2 arm — so for T in [623.15 K, 863.15 K) a point at exactly p = p_B23(T) routes to Region 3, not Region 2. (This start-inclusivity predates op-cv1c, which only closed the upper edge.) The measured practical effect is small — at (623.15 K, 100 MPa) the two region equations differ by 3.245e-6 in h and 1.769e-5 in v — but one of the two statements is wrong and should be settled against the IF97 release, then the loser corrected.

3. Minor contract mismatch, same audit: ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs::is_outside_pressure_range PANICS on an out-of-range pressure while its ph_flash_eqm twin RETURNS true. Both are named as predicates and both are called as 'if is_outside_pressure_range(p) { panic!(...) }', so the ps version can never return true and its caller's panic is dead code with a worse message.
title: tampines-steam-tables: region router accepts p = 0 Pa and the B23 line contradicts its own doc

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

**Flare is a first-class refinery system, not an infinite sink.** A sink that
silently absorbs whatever is sent to it will hide exactly the conservation
failures this programme is built to expose.

## Steady-state scope

```
routine vents / purge -> flare header -> KO drum -> flare
```

Track: mass flow; composition; liquid knockout; combustion products; emissions.

## Later transient scope

```
unit trip -> PSV / depressurization -> relief network -> KO drum -> flare
```

Selected transient hydraulics may later use Outram-FOAM.

**Do not CFD the flare flame as part of the ordinary steady-state flowsheet.**

Flare carbon and sulfur are explicit terms in the refinery-wide balances and
must not be aggregated into "losses".

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Flare and relief system

description:
FOUND while building the steam_table_plotter GUI (op-eebe, GH issue #26).

WHERE
crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/pt_flash_eqm/mod.rs,
region_fwd_eqn_single_phase.

For temperature in (623.15 K, 647.096 K) and pressure between p_sat(T) and
p_B23(T), the match arm

    (623.15..=863.15).contains(&temp) && (0.0..=p_boundary_23_pascal).contains(&pres)
        => FwdEqnRegion::Region2

fires. But at p > p_sat(T) in that temperature band the fluid is COMPRESSED
LIQUID, which is IAPWS-IF97 Region 3, not Region 2. The B23 line only separates
Region 2 from Region 3 ABOVE the critical temperature / outside the two-phase
region; below T_crit the saturation line is the relevant boundary on the liquid
side and it sits well below p_B23.

CONSEQUENCE
h_tp_eqm_single_phase / s_tp_eqm_single_phase evaluate near-critical compressed
liquid through the Region 2 vapour equations, which is an extrapolation.
checked::try_* does not catch it -- the (T,p) pair is inside the declared
envelope, so it returns Ok with an extrapolated value.

NOT QUANTIFIED. This was identified by reading the region dispatch while
working out where the plotter could and could not trust the library; no error
magnitude was measured, and it may be small. Do not treat the numbers as
established until someone measures them against the published table (the
240-300 bar single-phase fixtures in
src/interfaces/tests_and_examples/pt_flash_steam_table/ would be the place).

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (plotter only)
examples/steam_table_plotter/curves.rs::isobar stops the sub-critical
compressed-liquid branch at 623.15 K instead of running it up to T_sat(p), so
sub-critical isobars above about 165 bar show a visible break rather than an
extrapolated curve. That is documented in the curves.rs module header.

RELATED: op-hidb (a separate, and much larger, near-critical Region 3 defect in
x_ph_flash's saturated-liquid sub-region chain).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-20, ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. This bead's own text
already flagged the number as "NOT QUANTIFIED... do not treat as established
until someone measures it against the published table" -- I did that
measurement and it contradicts the bead.

I implemented the described fix (use p_sat(T) instead of p_boundary_2_3(T)
as the Region2/Region3 split for 623.15 K <= T < T_c = 647.096 K) and it
FAILS the crate's own reference-table tests. Concretely, at T=633.15 K,
p=18 MPa (a real row from the crate's single_phase_table_180_bar fixture,
p between B23(633.15K)=17.663 MPa and p_sat(633.15K)=18.666 MPa -- i.e.
exactly the band this bead claims is misclassified):

  - ORIGINAL code (uses B23 as the sole boundary): region = Region3,
    cp_tp_3(633.15K, 18MPa) = 15.82... kJ/kgK, matching the published
    reference table to within the test's 1e-3 relative tolerance (PASSES).
  - "FIXED" code (uses p_sat as the boundary below T_c): region = Region2,
    cp_tp_2(633.15K, 18MPa) = 15.860417 kJ/kgK, off by ~0.25% -- FAILS the
    same test, plus 5 more single_phase_table tests at 180-220 bar covering
    the same near-critical pressure band (all reverted cleanly by
    `git checkout` on this file; 11/11 single_phase_table_20_bar_to_220_bar
    tests pass again with the original B23-only logic restored).

So the physical picture in my "fix" was backwards. B23(T) rises SLOWER than
p_sat(T) as T increases from 623.15 K (they coincide exactly at 623.15 K,
16.529 MPa, then diverge: at 633.15 K, B23=17.663 MPa < p_sat=18.666 MPa).
The sliver between them is evidently still correctly Region 3 per IAPWS-IF97
-- B23 is not simply "the true saturation curve, valid only above Tc" as I
assumed; it is IF97's own chosen practical boundary between the Region 2 and
Region 3 backward-equation domains at every T from 623.15 K up, independent
of where the true two-phase dome sits. My reasoning that "Region 1 doesn't
extend above 623.15 K, so anything above p_sat there must be Region 3, and
therefore Region 2 must stop at p_sat too" does not follow -- IAPWS clearly
intends a band of single-phase vapour (still below the true p_sat) to be
evaluated with Region 3's equations instead of Region 2's, for accuracy
reasons this bead's author did not have when writing the original diagnosis.

CLOSING as investigated / not a defect. region_fwd_eqn_single_phase's
original code is reverted to unchanged and is correct as far as this
crate's own reference-table coverage can show. If a future reader has an
IAPWS-IF97 citation showing an actual bug in the B23-only dispatch, reopen
with that citation and a specific counter-example row, not a re-derivation
from first principles the way this bead's original text did.

title: tampines-steam-tables: region_fwd_eqn_single_phase classifies compressed liquid above 623.15 K as Region 2

description:
Measured 2026-08-12 during op-62vf. Not a defect, but it bounds what benchmarks are affordable and it should be known before someone budgets an Edwards or Marviken run.

MEASURED: a 24-cell, 20-outer-corrector blowdown ran 10002 steps (300 ms of simulated time at dt = 30 us) in roughly 200 s wall clock, release mode. That is about 20 ms per step, or 0.83 ms per cell per step. At 8 cells and 10 correctors the demonstrator test runs 667 steps in about 7 s.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (not profiled -- this is a reading of the code, and profiling is the first task):
1. InterfacialExchange::sources_with_properties allocates. Its doc comment already warns of this: outram_foam_multiphase::Phase carries scalar density and viscosity as per-phase constants with no setters, so BOTH phases plus a TwoFluidSystem plus several VolScalarFields are rebuilt from scratch for every cell on every outer corrector. In a blowdown the density changes every cell every step, so the rebuild cannot be cached.
2. IF97 calls per cell per corrector: one SaturatedProperties::at, sometimes a SaturatedTransport::at (four evaluations, one of them the R15-11 conductivity with its critical enhancement), and up to four PhaseState inversions, each a bracketed Illinois iteration.
3. The outer-corrector loop repeats 2 in full, up to n_outer_correctors times.

CHEAPEST LIKELY WINS, in order:
- Hoist the per-cell property work that does not depend on the pressure iterate out of the corrector loop.
- Give outram_foam_multiphase::Phase setters for rho and mu so the single-cell scratch system can be mutated rather than rebuilt (this is an upstream-crate change and needs its own bead if pursued).
- Reduce the default corrector count now that the loop is a proper Newton iteration on the volume residual: the demonstrator converges in 10 and often fewer, so 8 may already be generous.

DO NOT optimise before profiling, and do not trade accuracy for speed without re-running the whole two_fluid_tests battery -- several of its assertions are at 1e-13 and would catch a silent change.
title: tampines TwoFluid1d: six-equation march is slow -- roughly 20 ms per step at 24 cells with 20 outer correctors

description:
The instruction file uploaded alongside the API docs, telling the external agent how to write code for this workspace. Hardcoded in Rust (a const/template), not read from the workspace CLAUDE.md -- the root CLAUDE.md is ~600 lines of Claude Code harness policy (beads, hooks, working hours, push rules) that is noise to a chat agent and would eat the budget.

MUST CARRY (the rules that change the CODE it writes):
- Rust design rules: NO trait objects (Box<dyn>/&dyn/Arc<dyn>) -- enums for dispatch; NO Box<T>; NO lifetime parameters -- own by value or Arc<T>; Arc<RwLock<T>> for shared mutable state, Arc<T> for read-only, RwLock over Mutex, no channels for simulation state.
- uom typing throughout, with named type aliases rather than raw Quantity<...>.
- Human interface layer: every public item documented, what physical quantity, valid ranges, units spelled out even when uom-typed.
- V&V documentation: any test checking physics against a reference must state METHODOLOGY AND MEASURED RESULTS with uncertainty and date.
- Release mode for builds/tests.
- Reuse before writing: this is a 40-crate workspace and the prior is 'it already exists'.
- Intended use is education/research/V&V ONLY -- never reactor operation, control, licensing, or safety-critical decisions.
- AI output is untrusted draft until a human reviews it.

MUST STATE WHAT THE AGENT HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN -- the crates whose api.md is absent from the bundle, by name. An agent told nothing about them will infer they do not exist and invent APIs.

MUST NOT include: beads/kopi-beans workflow, git hooks, token accounting, the working-hours guardrail, push policy. None of it applies to a chat agent.
title: agent-docs: hardcoded AGENTS.md generator (the workspace rules for a remote agent)
